en.title: Elder Scrolls Online PC Copies Bundled with New Fantasy Novel
en.summary: A unique collaboration brings the world of Tamriel to a new audience. Grab a copy of Brigands & Breadknives and get a free PC version of The Elder Scrolls Online.
en.body:
In a rather delightful crossover, **Bethesda** has teamed up with UK publisher **Tor** to offer PC copies of **The Elder Scrolls Online** with the latest paperback release of **Brigands & Breadknives**. This title is the third installment in **Travis Baldree**'s popular "Legends and Lattes" series, known for its charming and low-stakes fantasy adventures. For eager fans, this partnership presents an exciting opportunity to dive into the expansive world of Tamriel, the setting for the beloved Elder Scrolls franchise, at no extra cost beyond the book's purchase price.

**The Elder Scrolls Online**, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game that has captivated players for over a decade, is typically priced around £15.99 on platforms like Steam. However, it has seen recent discounts, including a sale for £3.99 during **Bethesda**'s 40th Anniversary celebration. The bundled copies are available with all paperback editions of **Brigands & Breadknives** from major UK booksellers, including **Waterstones**, **Foyles**, and independent stores, with prices hovering around £10. Online retailers like Amazon UK also list the book for £8.49. The offer is specifically for the first print run, ensuring availability across most retailers in the UK. Participating bookstores are also distributing special branded bookmarks that contain a secondary code, unlocking an exclusive "Pink Torchbug" pet within **The Elder Scrolls Online**. To claim the game, customers need to enter the code found on a sticker within the novel via **Tor**'s dedicated redemption page. This promotion is capped at the first 10,000 sign-ups, adding a sense of urgency for those interested.

## A Bridge Between Cozy Fantasy and Epic Adventures

**Tor** described this collaboration as a perfect blend for "cosy fantasy book lovers and gamers," aiming to encourage readers to transition from the narrative of **Brigands & Breadknives** into forging their own adventures within the vast continent of Tamriel. This initiative is particularly noteworthy as **The Elder Scrolls Online** continues to be a flagship title for **Bethesda** and now **Xbox**, consistently receiving new expansions and content updates years after its initial launch. It serves as an accessible gateway for readers who might not have previously considered an MMORPG, offering a familiar fantasy setting and a welcoming community.

## What This Means for Players and Readers

This partnership is a clever move to broaden the player base for **The Elder Scrolls Online** while simultaneously promoting new literary works. For fans of **Travis Baldree**'s "Legends and Lattes" series, it offers a tangible reward that aligns with their existing interests. It taps into the growing popularity of "cozy gaming" and "cozy fantasy," genres that emphasize comfort, charm, and less intense challenges. This cross-promotion could introduce a significant number of new players to **ESO**, potentially revitalizing interest and encouraging further engagement with the game's extensive lore and ongoing narrative. The inclusion of a unique in-game pet adds an extra layer of appeal for existing **ESO** players who enjoy collecting cosmetic items.

## What's Next

The offer is tied to the first print run of **Brigands & Breadknives** and is limited to 10,000 redemptions. Players interested in claiming their free PC copy of **The Elder Scrolls Online** should act quickly to ensure they secure a code.

content_raw: Bethesda has announced it's partnering with a UK publisher, Tor, to bundle free PC copies of The Elder Scrolls Online with Travis Baldree's new paperback release of Brigands & Breadknives , the third entry into Baldree's "Legends and Lattes" fantasy series. The longstanding MMORPG, which has been ongoing for around 12 years, typically sells for £15.99 on Steam , but has also recently been on sale for £3.99 as part of Bethesda's 40th Anniversary sale . The free codes for ESO are available on all printed copies of the Brigands & Breadknives' paperback release at most UK-based bookstores, such as Waterstones, Foyles and local independents for around £10, or via online retailers like Amazon for £8.49 . At the time of publication, Amazon's UK listing has not been updated with any information regarding The Elder Scrolls Online. IGN reached out to Tor and Bethesda for clarification on this, and we've been told that the "free copy of [The Elder Scrolls Online] is on the whole first print run" and thus is "available from all retailers, including Amazon" in the UK. For those who prefer to shop local, participating bookshops are also handing out branded bookmarks containing a secondary code that unlocks a "Pink Torchbug" pet for use in ESO as well. After purchasing the novel, readers can enter the codes printed on the sticker through Tor's redemption page to claim the game , limited to the first 10,000 sign-ups. Announcing the collaboration with Bethesda, Tor described it as a partnership for "cosy fantasy book lovers and gamers", encouraging readers to move from Baldree's latest story into creating their own adventure in Tamriel. The Elder Scrolls Online remains one of Bethesda, and now Xbox's, biggest ongoing titles more than a decade after launch, continuing to receive expansions and regular content updates while attracting new players through subscription services, sales, and now, apparently, bookshops. Fans have also recently been reassured by Zenimax and Microsoft that, despite a recent round of layoffs across Xbox, ESO will continue and isn't on the verge of being shut down. Bethesda is also continuing to support its other big IP, Fallout. Remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas are in the works in addition to a new Fallout game from Obsidian Entertainment. Bethesda has also entered pre-production on Fallout 5 , likely to ensure the team can make the jump to it after The Elder Scrolls 6 is finished. Robert Anderson is IGN's Senior Commerce Editor and resident deals expert on games, collectibles, trading card games, and more. You can follow him @robertliam21 on Bluesky .
